newsitem.title: UK: London's AIM to change listing rules for clarity.
newsitem.headline: London's AIM to change listing rules for clarity.

text.p: The London Stock Exchange plans to change some of the rules for admission to its Alternative Investment Market (AIM) to bring greater clarity and provide potential investors with more information.
An exchange news release said the proposed modifications were sent to market users on Wednesday for comment and confirmation. They are due to take effect in 28 days time.
Applicants to AIM, the market for small and growing companies, will be required to give prior notification at least 10 business days before their intended date of admission, the exchange said.
"This will allow the market more time to make investment decisions," it added.
The exchange also announced measures to enhance the transparency of the market.

The requirement for major shareholders' disclosure in the admission document will decrease from 10 percent to three percent or more. The publication date for risk trades is to be reduced to three days from five.

The exchange said companies would no longer be suspended during a reverse takeover of another AIM company. "In these circumstances there is sufficient information about both companies in the public domain to allow the effects of the takeover to be assessed," it said.
Another change recommended is an amplification of the investor "risk warning" and the requirement that it should be carried more prominently on all admission documents.
